findings.description: The shipped script omits the Group 2 (Google Maps - HERE WeGo) code ('hence code is omitted', line 762-765) but later shipped code depends on objects it would create (GMHWG, HWGTask*SuccessfulTime). Run as shipped, 86 of 418 top-level expressions fail from line 771 onward; Fig. 7, Table 2, Table 4 (GM-HWG, BM-HWG), Table 5, Section 4.5 Fligner test and Table 9 GM/HWG rows cannot be produced by the shipped code. The README states the script reproduces the analysis only partially.
findings.evidence: outputs/runs.json (lossless.still_failing; first: line 771 object 'GMHWG' not found)
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the complete Group 2 code block, including the missing-value handling for GM_HWG.csv.

findings.description: Table 8 BM-HWG Wilcoxon W for SUS scores: the shipped code yields W = 1137.5; the paper reports W = 1037.5. The p-value (<.001) and 95% CI [12.5, 30.0] produced by the same test match, so the gap is in the reported statistic only (pattern consistent with a transcription error; not adjudicated).
findings.suggested_fix: Authors to confirm the W statistic in Table 8.

findings.description: GM_HWG.csv contains 5 empty task-success cells; the handling is undocumented. Setting them to 0 (the convention the shipped code applies to STAT.csv, line 127) reproduces every Group 2 value; keeping them as NA, as a literal mirror of the Group 1 code would, gives discrepant values (e.g. Fig. 7 HWG mean 2.18 vs 2.11, Table 4 GM-HWG V 198 vs 281).
findings.suggested_fix: Document and code the missing-value rule for the task files.

findings.description: Execution-order defect: line 776 (SUS_GMDiff) uses SUS_ScoresGroup1/2, defined only at lines 1075-1086. It ran only on the reviewer's second pass, which re-tried failed expressions after the whole script.
findings.evidence: outputs/logs/lossless_exprlog.csv (pass 1 fail, pass 2 ok at line 776)
findings.suggested_fix: Move the Section 4.5 block after the SUS block.

findings.description: The script calls View() twice (lines 22, 126); under non-interactive Rscript this is fatal ('X11 is not available'), so the byte-identical script stops at line 22. Commenting them out is lossless and was the only edit to shipped code.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove View() calls or guard them with if (interactive()).

findings.description: SUS_GMCorrelation (SUS vs GM score, Table 9) is overwritten at line 1511 by a STAT vs GM score test; the reviewer recomputed the Table 9 SUS-GM value with the test as defined at line 1402.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicated block at lines 1511-1527.

findings.description: Hygiene: Table 3 uses hard-coded HERE WeGo success counts (19, 24, 11, 14, 10), which agree with GM_HWG.csv after empty cells are set to 0; STAT.csv header typo 'Partiicipant_ID'; leading space in Participants.csv Maps_Used (handled by trim_ws); rows are joined across files by position, not by participant ID; paper cites figshare v2 while the link given is v1 (files are byte-identical).
findings.suggested_fix: Compute counts from data; merge on Participant_ID.

limitations: The shipped script cannot run end to end (Group 2 code omitted), hence 'technical failure'. Of 160 reported numbers, 90 were produced by the shipped code (with View() commented out); 70 needed a reviewer-written Group 2 block. Counts: {"match": 159, "discrepant": 1, "not_checkable": 1}.
Group 2 values depend on a reviewer choice (empty GM_HWG.csv cells = 0); the NA-kept alternative is reported per value.
Figures 1-6 were regenerated and inspected for plausibility; they were not compared pixel-by-pixel with the published figures.
Run used R 4.4.3 from conda-forge, not the authors' 2022 R; package versions drift (see environment.json).
The prompt's rule-pack and schema URLs (lukasroeseler.github.io/reprocrowd/...) returned HTTP 404; the forrtproject.github.io copies were used.
No nanopublications were published; nanopubs/PUBLISHED.md lists the planned chain without URIs.
github_url points at the ReproCrowd repository; this bundle has not been pushed there.
The scientific conclusions were not assessed; robustness not checked.
